To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

retinoic acid (RA) is a potent inducer of cell differentiation, and that the biological effects of RA are mediated through the RA receptor (RAR) family of nuclear receptors, which are ligand-activated transcription factors.

(a) the RAR/RXR heterodimers are the functional units of RA signaling; (b) the ligand dependent transactivating function (AF2) of the RAR/RXRs is located at their carboxyl terminal end; and (c) the AF2s of the RAR isotypic heterodimers differ in their ligand binding properties, their transactivation potential, and their sensitivity to the corepressors.

the retinoic acid receptor (RAR) family of transcription factors is encoded by three genes that generate at least eight isoforms, each of which can bind to the same response elements in the promoter regions of retinoid-responsive genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of the retinoid receptors and with their functional role in the regulation of gene expression.
the molecular biology of nuclear hormone receptors.
the molecular mechanisms by which RA regulates the expression of specific genes in different cell types.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molecular mechanisms of retinoid action, although far from being fully understood, have been clarified to a considerable extent.
the molecular basis for the biological effects of RA is still not fully understood, and that many questions are left unanswered.

RAR and RXR are ligand activated nuclear receptors that bind to RA response elements in a ligand dependent manner and that they regulate the expression of RA target genes in a ligand, tissue, and cell dependent manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to identify a new family of nuclear hormone receptors, which is now called the retinoic acid receptor family.
the RAR/RXRs are the key to the understanding of the molecular basis for the biological effects of retinoid signaling.
we have shown that the RARs and RARs are the receptors for RA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RAR and RXR receptors are the key components of the retinoid signaling pathway and the molecular basis of their pleiotropic functions.
there are a number of factors that contribute to the ability of a cell to undergo a differentiation response to retinoids.
there is a lot of diversity in the way that different cell types respond to RA.
